stem:
Meena snaps a bar magnet into two equal pieces while doing an experiment at home in Jaipur. She says, "Now one small piece will have only a North pole and the other only a South pole."
What does she actually find when she tests each piece?

options.text: Each small piece has both a North pole and a South pole.
One piece has only a North pole and the other only a South pole.
Both pieces lose their magnetism completely.
Only the bigger piece keeps its poles; the smaller piece has none.

teacher.key_rationale: Breaking a magnet always produces smaller magnets, each with a North and a South pole; isolated single poles cannot be obtained. Hence A is correct.
